$comment: Every entry names a test and the ONE-LINE change to production source that must
make it go red. `make test-mutation` applies each change, runs the named gate,
and fails if the gate still passes — because a test that survives the deletion of
the code it claims to pin is asserting something else.
This exists because three tests landed in #321 that passed for the wrong reason,
and every one was caught by doing this by hand: an oracle case that threw inside
its own setup and so printed identical output on both runtimes, a property suite
that compared zero inputs after a NaN run count, and an event-loop test whose
timer handed platform_poll a positive timeout, which counts as progress by itself
and so never produced the no-progress tick under test. Doing it by hand depends on
remembering to; this does not.
Fields:
name    what the mutation proves, in the form '<test> dies when <code> is broken'
why     one sentence: the defect this catches if the mutation survives
source  production file to patch (never a test file)
find    exact string to replace; must appear EXACTLY once (the runner checks)
replace what to put there — usually the pre-fix code, or a deleted guard
gate    how to observe red; see GATE KINDS in scripts/run-mutations.mjs
expect_detail  substring the RED output must contain; '' is a visible opt-out
(`rebuild` is gone: it was derivable from the gate kind, and a run filtered to
only `make:` entries then skipped the restore build and left bin/lava holding
the mutated source with a clean git tree and a success message.)

mutations.name: 55-encoding-pollution V dies when the utf-8 decode return path goes back through .call
mutations.why: A replaced Function.prototype.call substitutes decode()'s return value outright, so decode() hands back an ArrayBuffer instead of a string.

mutations.name: 55-encoding-pollution U dies when toBytes reads the view window live
mutations.why: A poisoned byteOffset/byteLength pair selects a window across the shared allocUnsafe pool, so decode() returns a neighbouring Buffer's bytes.

mutations.name: 55-encoding-pollution W dies when toBytes brands with instanceof
mutations.why: Ctor[Symbol.hasInstance] is a configurable own property, so the brand is forgeable in both directions and misroutes the input into the wrong arm.

mutations.name: 13-structured-clone dies when the DataView clone arm reads its window live
mutations.why: structuredClone copies the whole backing buffer and re-slices the copy, so a poisoned window exposes pool neighbours in the clone.
mutations.expect_detail: DataView clone window must not widen under a poisoned getter

mutations.name: 13-structured-clone dies when the DataView brand goes back to instanceof
mutations.why: A forged DataView[Symbol.hasInstance] misroutes a genuine DataView into the typed-array arm, where the captured getter rejects the receiver.
mutations.expect_detail: a forged hasInstance must not break a real DataView clone

mutations.name: run_until_idle_waits_out_a_stale_wakeup dies when a no-progress tick ends the drive
mutations.why: A surplus wakeup byte ends the drive with an off-loop completion still in flight, and it returns the did_work an earlier tick latched — so it reports success.

mutations.name: the detector's fixtures die when isWrite swallows read-modify-write again
mutations.why: Compound, logical and update assignments all run GetValue before PutValue, so exempting them lets the ratchet pay out for rewriting a counted read as `??=`.

mutations.why: PropertyDefinition is in FUNCTION_TYPES but has no .params, so `class C { x = String; }` crashed the whole scan on valid syntax.

mutations.name: the baseline tests die when the per-class comparison collapses into a total
mutations.why: A file that fixes one accessor and gains one live global has an unchanged total, and per-class baselines exist precisely so that cannot pass.

mutations.name: the poisoned http-smoke phases die when a framing validator goes back to re.test
mutations.why: Content-Length framing. With the check on a live regex, a poisoned exec answered 200 OK for `Content-Length: abc` — parseInt gives NaN and the body framing desyncs. The charCode form has no regex to poison at all.

mutations.name: the poisoned http-smoke phases die when the chunked check goes back to re.test
mutations.why: Transfer-Encoding framing. A steered check accepted `gzip` as chunked, which is the other half of the smuggling pair.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when SURVIVED is not reported
mutations.why: Inverting this branch makes every surviving mutation read as a kill, which is the exact P0 a review found: a gate whose value is its honesty, with nothing checking that honesty.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when WRONG REASON stops being enforced
mutations.why: This branch IS 82d8a0e. Without it a mutation that breaks something unrelated is reported as killed, which is how a mis-escaped replacement once looked like it worked.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when the green-baseline check is removed
mutations.why: Without it the gate reports a kill for a target that was already failing, so 'it went red' proves nothing.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when a stale entry becomes a silent skip
mutations.why: A manifest entry that no longer describes the code must fail; skipping it drops the coverage the gate exists to guarantee.

mutations.name: 54-url-pollution X1 dies when endsInANumber goes back to a live re.test
mutations.why: Steered true, '4x' reads as numeric and parseInt gives 4, so http://1.2.3.4x/ silently becomes http://1.2.3.4/ — a host substitution.

mutations.name: 54-url-pollution X2 dies when the %2f check goes back to a live re.test
mutations.why: The path-traversal guard, in the direction that discriminates: a steered validator makes a legitimate path look encoded and throws where node returns one.

mutations.name: the Lava-only regexp pollution test dies when the header-name validator goes back to re.test
mutations.why: node ACCEPTS 'X-Evil: 1\r\nInjected' under this poison (undici's validator is JS), so this deviation cannot be oracled and CLAUDE.md section 1 requires a Lava-only pin.

mutations.name: the Lava-only regexp pollution test dies when the header trim goes back to a global replaceAll
mutations.why: A global replace under a forged exec does not answer wrongly — it never returns, because lastIndex only advances on an empty match. The observable effect IS the hang, so the recorded reason is the timeout verdict: before capture() bounded it this entry ate 3m16s and multi-GB in CI and degraded to WRONG REASON on a memory-capped runner.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when util.js drops the single-argument guard
mutations.why: Without it util.format folds %% even with one argument, where node returns the string verbatim. Pinned separately from console.js because the two are different implementations and one entry would fake coverage of both.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when console.js drops the single-argument guard
mutations.why: console.js has its own formatter — it is the bootstrap prelude and has no require to delegate with — so removing util.js's guard leaves console.log correct and vice versa. This entry moves the raw console.log rows, a different line range from the util entry.

mutations.name: the poisoned http-smoke phases die when Content-Length conversion reads live parseInt
mutations.why: A sound allChars digit check next to live parseInt still desyncs framing: contentLengthRemaining becomes the gadget value. Poison-before-require is the realistic order; bootstrap capture on primordials is the fix. The Odin pi= pin covers the eager URL port path; this entry covers the lazy http framing path.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution targeted dies when the export-default name comes back through .match
mutations.why: String.prototype.match re-reads R.exec off the receiver, so the declared name is attacker-chosen and the transform interpolates it into the emitted module body as an identifier — code injection, not a wrong answer.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution blunt dies when the keyword boundary test goes back to a regex
mutations.why: A forged exec makes /[\w$]/.test answer true for every character, so keywordAt rejects every import and export and the emitted source keeps raw module syntax JSC cannot parse.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution charcodeat dies when the mask reads code units live
mutations.why: Routing the scanner off charAt onto charCodeAt is only a fix if the read is captured: a gadget lying about quote characters makes a string body scan as code, so text the module wrote as DATA is spliced out and re-emitted.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution arrayat dies when the mask stack is read through Array.prototype.at
mutations.why: The mode stack decides whether the scanner is inside a template literal; a forged at(-1) answering 'code' means it never enters template mode and statement-shaped template text becomes code.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution json dies when emitted literals go back through the live JSON.stringify
mutations.why: Every string literal in the generated CommonJS — require specifiers, export keys, __filename/__dirname/import.meta.url — is produced here, so a replaced stringify writes the emitted source directly.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution tail dies when the export result object inherits from Object.prototype
mutations.why: transformExport carries an own `tail` on one of eight return shapes; without a null prototype the other seven read Object.prototype.tail and join it into the emitted source, so a data-only merge gadget is code execution in the module body.
mutations.find: return { __proto__: null, body: decl + ';' + assigns, tail: null };

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution join dies when the wrapper is assembled with a live Array.prototype.join
mutations.why: The joins assemble the emitted module, so a gadget lying only for the '\n' separator replaces the WHOLE output rather than one interpolated identifier — a strictly larger win than the export-default carrier. Mutating the capture rather than one call site keeps esm.js syntactically valid, so the gate measures the carrier and not a bootstrap parse error.

mutations.name: 58-esm-pollution strglobal dies when the source coercion reads the live String global
mutations.why: transform() coerces its `source` argument with String(); the existing json entry reverts JSONStringify and StringG on one line, so the String capture on this line was never proven on its own.

mutations.name: 29-esm-transform-edge dies when findStmtEnd drops the seenMeaningful flag
mutations.why: The old code got this from `'+-*/%=<>&|^,.?:('.indexOf('')` returning 0, so a newline before any meaningful character continued the statement; without the flag an import whose clause starts on the next line ends early and reports an unsupported form.

mutations.name: 29-esm-transform-edge dies when import.meta is rewritten by searching the source, not the mask
mutations.why: The mask blanks strings and comments, so searching it leaves an `import.meta` written inside a string literal alone; searching the source rewrites it to __import_meta and silently corrupts module data.

mutations.name: 29-esm-transform-edge dies when isSpace narrows to ASCII
mutations.why: The `\s*` strips these helpers replace accept the full ES whitespace set; narrowing to ASCII makes `export const<NBSP>name` emit the key "const", which is a silent behavior change the comment explicitly warns against.

mutations.name: 29-esm-transform-edge dies when the identifier class drops `$`
mutations.why: No other fixture uses `$`, `_` or digits in a binding name, so the `$` arm of the code-unit predicate that replaced [A-Za-z_$] was unexercised and could be dropped without any test noticing.

mutations.name: 59-global-replace-hangs dies when querystring's '+' decode goes back to a global replace
mutations.why: parse is public node:querystring and a single '+' in a query string reaches it, so a server doing parse(req.url.split('?')[1]) wedges on a crafted request: a global replace under a forged exec only advances lastIndex on an empty match and never returns. node answers correctly under the same poison, so this is a Lava-only defect.

mutations.name: regexp_pollution_immunity glob dies when matchesGlob strips backslashes with a global replace
mutations.why: Both arguments are caller-supplied, and the global replace spins under a forged exec. node hangs here too, so this is a deviation in Lava's favour and cannot be an oracle case.

mutations.name: regexp_pollution_immunity inspect dies when the Buffer hex grouping goes back to a global replace
mutations.why: console.log(buf) on a Buffer holding remote bytes reaches this; the global replace spins under a forged exec. node hangs here too.

mutations.name: regexp_pollution_immunity blob dies when native line endings go back to a global replace
mutations.why: new Blob([text], {endings:'native'}) runs this over caller text; the global replace spins under a forged exec. node hangs here too.

mutations.name: regexp_pollution_immunity debuglog dies when NODE_DEBUG is compiled by chained global replaces
mutations.why: Three global replaces run on the FIRST debuglog call, so the process wedges at the point it tries to emit a diagnostic. Lava-only because Lava has no process.stderr, so the outputs cannot match node however the spin is fixed.

mutations.name: 59-global-replace-hangs mime dies when the MIME value escape goes back to a global replace
mutations.why: MIMEType#toString is reachable from a remote Content-Type and node answers correctly under the same poison, so this is a Lava-only spin of the same tier as the querystring bug. The merge gate found it after the first pass claimed the class was closed.

mutations.name: regexp_pollution_immunity puny dies when the RFC 3490 separator fold goes back to a global replace
mutations.why: punycode.toASCII on a caller-supplied hostname spun; node hangs identically so it cannot be an oracle case. Pins availability only, because other live .test reads in punycode.js still steer the per-label encode decision.

mutations.name: regexp_pollution_immunity dbg-nodot dies when the NODE_DEBUG escaper stops escaping '.'
mutations.why: Nothing observed debugEnvPattern's OUTPUT before: the poisoned probe passes with NODE_DEBUG unset, i.e. when the function is never called. Dropping the '.' branch makes 'a.b' enable 'axb', which is the escape the compile exists to do.

mutations.name: stdio-write dies when the writer stops retrying a partial/EAGAIN write
mutations.why: os.write abandons its loop on any errno and the old caller discarded n and err, so a full non-blocking pipe ended the write and reported success: console.log('x'.repeat(300000)) delivered 65536 bytes and exited 0. The flag is inherited from the parent, which is why an ordinary shell pipe never reproduces it. expect_detail keys off the assertion text, not the byte count: the truncated count depends on how fast the reader drains and was measured at both 65536 and 196608.
mutations.replace: if werr != nil do return written, werr

mutations.name: 61-stdio-lifecycle dies when pipe() stops excluding the stdio singletons
mutations.why: Without node's `dest !== process.stdout/stderr` exclusion, `src.pipe(process.stdout)` calls end() on a process-lifetime singleton. Note what the assertion keys off: since `_destroy` undoes the teardown, the stream RECOVERS a tick later, so `writable` reads true either way and only the spurious 'finish' event proves end() was reached. Before that half existed this dropped every later write and raised 'write after end'.
expect_detail: pipe() must not even reach end(), so no finish

mutations.name: stdio-lifecycle dies when pipe() stops excluding the stdio singletons (pipe shape)
mutations.why: Same defect as the compat entry, gated on the node:test so both fd shapes are covered — node's stdout is a different class on a pipe. The script counts 'finish' events rather than comparing bytes, because the recovery makes the bytes identical with the exclusion deleted; a byte-only version of this test SURVIVED this mutation.
expect_detail: lava must match node on a pipe

mutations.name: stdio-lifecycle dies when _destroy stops undoing the teardown
mutations.why: node's stdio _destroy is a dummy that runs the callback and then calls _undestroy(). Drop the undo and a single process.stdout.end() anywhere in a dependency is permanent: the stream stays ended for the rest of the run and silently drops every later write. Gated on the node:test, not the oracle case: recovery is only observable when the harness controls the fd shape, and the compat harness always gives a case a file.
expect_detail: lava must match node byte-for-byte on a file

mutations.name: stdio-lifecycle dies when _undestroy stops clearing the ending flag
mutations.why: The `writable` getter is `!destroyed && !ending`, so leaving `ending` set makes the stream report unwritable forever even though destroyed was cleared — the recovery looks applied and is not. Pins the individual field, not just the presence of the call.
expect_detail: lava must match node byte-for-byte on a file

mutations.name: stdio-lifecycle dies when the stdio stream pins autoDestroy/emitClose off
mutations.why: The recovery is reached THROUGH autoDestroy (end() -> 'finish' -> destroy() -> _undestroy). Setting autoDestroy:false — as the first revision of this file did — leaves _destroy unreached, so end() is permanent even with the dummy in place, and 'close' never fires.
mutations.replace: ReflectApply(Writable, this, [{ decodeStrings: false, autoDestroy: false, emitClose: false }]);
expect_detail: lava must match node byte-for-byte on a file

mutations.name: 61-stdio-lifecycle dies when the _isStdio marker is dropped
mutations.why: node sets an own _isStdio on both singletons and its own stream/net code feature-detects on it, so ecosystem code reads it too. Absent, a library's 'is this stdio?' check silently takes the wrong branch.

mutations.name: fs_write_payload dies when the buffer length is sampled before the window getters
mutations.why: byteOffset/byteLength on a DataView may be OWN accessors, so reading them runs arbitrary JS that can resize the backing ArrayBuffer. Sampling the buffer's length first validates the window against a size that no longer exists, and the resolver hands back a slice past the allocation — 4088 bytes of out-of-bounds heap written into a caller-named file.

ab_len := f64(jsc.JSObjectGetArrayBufferByteLength(ctx, ab, nil))
				off_f := jsc.JSValueToNumber(ctx, get_named(ctx, obj, "byteOffset"), nil)
				len_f := jsc.JSValueToNumber(ctx, get_named(ctx, obj, "byteLength"), nil)

mutations.name: stdio_fd_guard dies when the fd is converted before it is compared
mutations.why: `this.fd` is a plain writable property, so process.stdout.fd = 1.5 reaches this native. A float->int conversion is undefined in Odin for NaN, +/-Inf and out-of-range values, and truncation lands 1.5 and 2.9 squarely on fd 1 and 2 — so converting first turns the guard into a no-op for exactly the values it exists to catch. NaN and Infinity do NOT catch this on x86 (cvttsd2si yields INT_MIN, rejected either way), which is why the fractional cases are in the list.

switch {
	case fd_num == 1:
		target = os.stdout
	case fd_num == 2:
		target = os.stderr
mutations.replace:
fd_int := int(fd_num)
	switch fd_int {
	case 1:
		target = os.stdout
	case 2:
		target = os.stderr

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when the read result is not re-tagged as a Buffer
mutations.why: The native returns a plain Uint8Array where node returns a Buffer. Without the re-tag, Buffer.isBuffer is false and `.toString('hex')` falls through to Uint8Array.prototype.toString — comma-joined decimals instead of hex, with no throw. That shipped for a year.

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when the encoding is dropped instead of decoded in JS
mutations.why: Reads must be decoded through Buffer's codecs here, because the native ignored the encoding argument entirely and decoded everything as UTF-8 — readFileSync(p,'hex') returned the file's text instead of its hex. expect_detail keys off a UNIQUE assertion message: an earlier version used ['strictEqual','string'], which appears in the red output of every failing assert.equal in the file and would have accepted a break of the Buffer re-tag instead.
mutations.find: return encoding === null ? buf : BufferPrototypeToString(buf, encoding);
expect_detail: an encoding must be decoded, not returned as a Buffer

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when an unknown encoding is not rejected
mutations.why: node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE for an unrecognized encoding. Without the check the name reaches Buffer#toString, which throws a differently-coded error, and a caller catching by code sees the wrong one. expect_detail keys off the error that ESCAPES (Buffer#toString's uncoded 'Unknown encoding: bogus'), not the code the case asserts: assert.throws swallows the mismatch into an AssertionError, so the coded name never reaches the diff.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when util.inspect stops quoting a top-level string
mutations.why: node's util.inspect QUOTES a top-level string ('x' -> "'x'") while console.log/format print a string ARGUMENT raw — format goes through stringify(), which short-circuits strings before inspect is reached, so the depth-0 raw arm had no caller left and was deleted. Restoring it un-quotes every message built with util.inspect, which is how fs.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE read `Received bogus`.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when inspect stops choosing the quote character
mutations.why: node picks the delimiter to avoid escaping — a string containing a single quote is rendered with DOUBLE quotes ("it's", not 'it\'s'). Always using single quotes escapes where node does not, so any inspected value containing an apostrophe differs.

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when the pristine Buffer capture moves back into fs.js
mutations.why: fs.js is a LAZY module, so a `require('buffer').Buffer` capture at its module-eval reads whatever user code left there — a dependency's top-level `require('buffer').Buffer = shim` then steers and discloses every fs read. loader.js snapshots it right after buffer is instantiated, where the ordering is provable.
expect_detail: must not observe the file contents

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when falsy encodings stop meaning binary
mutations.why: node's assertEncoding is guarded `if (encoding && ...)`, so '', false, 0 and NaN all return a Buffer. Rejecting them broke code that worked before the JS layer existed, because the native treated a non-string encoding as binary and returned data.
mutations.replace: if (encoding === null || encoding === undefined) return null;

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when 'buffer' is validated like an ordinary encoding
mutations.why: node's getOptions skips assertEncoding for 'buffer' so it reaches Buffer#toString and throws ERR_UNKNOWN_ENCODING. Validating it yields ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE — a different code AND message on a documented fs option value.

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE loses node's object branch
mutations.why: node's determineSpecificType renders an object receiver as `an instance of <Ctor>`, not `type object (<inspected>)`. The reachable trigger is fs.readFile(path, options) with a forgotten callback. expect_detail keys on the ESCAPING text (Received {}), not the case assertion: assert.throws re-surfaces the original TypeError on a message mismatch here, so the assertion text never reaches the diff.
mutations.find: if (typeof ctor === 'function' && ctor.name) return 'an instance of ' + ctor.name;

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when the Received string stops being truncated
mutations.why: node cuts a string longer than 28 chars to its first 25 plus '...' before inspecting it into the Received clause.

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when the read result is copied instead of shared
mutations.why: The zero-copy re-tag is a rank-2 memory claim on the hottest fs call there is. A copying Buffer.from(view) lands in the Buffer pool, so the result is an offset into a 256 KB store instead of an exact-size view. Before this entry the claim had NO test: the copying form left the whole case green.
expect_detail: must not be an offset into a pool

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when path type validation is dropped
mutations.why: node rejects a non string/Buffer/URL/fd path with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE; without the check an object is stringified and read as the filename '[object Object]'.
expect_detail: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'null'

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when the error callback regains its second argument
mutations.why: node calls the readFile error callback with exactly one argument; the native's completion always builds a 2-slot array, so passing data through makes arguments.length 2.
expect_detail: the error callback takes one argument on node

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when cb validation moves after options validation
mutations.why: node validates `callback || options` BEFORE the options, so readFile(p,'bogus') reports the string as a bad callback. The reverse order reports a plausible but different error for a forgotten callback.
mutations.find:
var cb = callback || options;
    if (typeof cb !== 'function') {

mutations.name: 62-fs-read-buffer dies when a function in the options slot is rejected
mutations.why: node's getOptions treats a callback sitting in the options slot as absent; rejecting it turns readFileSync(p, fn) from a working binary read into a throw.
mutations.find: if (options === null || options === undefined || typeof options === 'function') {

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when inspect drops node's ${ guard
mutations.why: node's strEscape refuses the backtick delimiter when the string contains '${', because inspect output is meant to read back as a literal and a backtick-delimited '${' is a live template substitution. Omitting the guard also regressed output that was CORRECT before the delimiter rule was introduced.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when the backtick branch is removed
mutations.why: A string containing both quote characters is backtick-delimited on node. The earlier manifest entry deleted the whole delimiter block, so it only proved the double-quote arm; deleting just this line survived the case.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when inspect stops escaping control characters
mutations.why: node's strEscape escapes the whole C0 range, DEL and C1. Leaving them raw makes an unescaped \x1B in any inspected value an ANSI-injection vector through the log line, which is why this is a security fix and not a rendering nicety.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when a lone surrogate is not escaped
mutations.why: node escapes an unpaired surrogate as \\udXXX; Lava used to hand it to the string conversion, which replaced it with U+FFFD — the value came back LOSSY, not merely rendered differently.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when Symbol.for is read off the captured Symbol object
mutations.why: Capturing `Symbol` alone is not enough — `.for` is a writable property on it, so a lazily-evaluated module reading P.Symbol.for at its own module-eval still reads whatever user code left there. The primordials table must expose the METHOD. Pinned through a Buffer, whose util.inspect.custom hook is looked up with that symbol: without it a Buffer renders as a plain Uint8Array. An earlier version of this entry SURVIVED because case 57 inspected no Buffer at all.

mutations.name: 64-stream-write dies when write() reports errors async instead of throwing
mutations.why: node throws ERR_STREAM_NULL_VALUES and ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE synchronously from write(). Routing them through writeErrorNextTick delivers the right code on the wrong turn, so `assert.throws(() => s.write(null))` passes under node and fails here.
mutations.replace: if (chunk === null) { writeErrorNextTick(this, errNullValues(), cb); return false; }

mutations.name: 64-stream-write dies when the accept set goes back to instanceof Uint8Array
mutations.why: `instanceof Uint8Array` is wrong in BOTH directions: it rejects DataView and Int16Array, which node accepts, and it accepts Object.create(Uint8Array.prototype), which node rejects. ArrayBuffer.isView is the whole test.
expect_detail: Receiver should be a typed array view

mutations.name: 64-stream-write dies when a view is not normalized to a Buffer
mutations.why: THE regression that got #326's attempt reverted. node hands _write a Buffer with encoding 'buffer' for every view; without the conversion `chunk.length` is undefined for a DataView, writableLength goes NaN, and 'drain' can never fire again because NaN === 0 is false.

mutations.name: 64-stream-write dies when Readable.push does not accept what write does
mutations.why: Widening only the writable half makes a PassThrough take a view on one side and error on the other — which is how the first attempt shipped. The replacement KEEPS the normalization so the entry pins the brand widening alone — changing both at once would leave a kill ambiguous about which half the case detects.
mutations.replace:
} else if (chunk instanceof Uint8Array) {
        chunk = bytesToBuffer(chunk);

mutations.name: 64-stream-write dies when the encoding is not validated before the chunk type
mutations.why: node validates an explicit encoding first, which is observable: write(5, 'bogus') reports ERR_UNKNOWN_ENCODING, not the chunk type.
expect_detail: must be of type string or an instance of Buffer

mutations.name: 64-stream-write dies when setDefaultEncoding accepts an unknown name
mutations.why: node throws ERR_UNKNOWN_ENCODING; accepting it silently poisons every later string write on the stream.

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when a module resolves Buffer itself instead of taking the loader's
mutations.why: net.js is a LAZY module, so its own require('buffer') runs on the user's first require of net — after user code. Node is not steerable this way; measured, sock.write('PAYLOAD') delivered "PAYLOAD" on node and "TAMPERED" here.
mutations.replace: var PristineBuffer = { Buffer: require('buffer').Buffer, from: require('buffer').Buffer.from, alloc: require('buffer').Buffer.alloc, concat: require('buffer').Buffer.concat, isBuffer: require('buffer').Buffer.isBuffer };
expect_detail: net must not resolve Buffer through the shim

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when Buffer.from is read off the constructor at call time
mutations.why: Capturing the CONSTRUCTOR is not enough: `.from` is a writable member read off it at call time, so `Buffer.from = evil` steers a module holding a pristine constructor. This is the half the first version of the fix missed — the object is not the method, the same lesson as Symbol.for in util.js.
mutations.replace: var BufferFrom = function (v, a, b) { return PristineBuffer.Buffer.from(v, a, b); };
expect_detail: a replaced Buffer.from must not steer net either

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when os.userInfo reads Buffer.from at call time
mutations.why: os.userInfo originally re-read the live export on EVERY call, so it was steerable at any time — a case that only swaps things before the first require cannot see it. This mutation restores a call-time read while leaving the module-eval capture intact, so it pins the call-time half alone.
mutations.replace: var BufferFrom = function (v, a, b) { return PristineBuffer.Buffer.from(v, a, b); };
expect_detail: os must not read Buffer.from at call time

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when http.js resolves Buffer itself
mutations.why: http.js was migrated with NO test behind it: reverting this one line left every gate green while the measured divergence returned. Two of five migrated modules were unpinned until this entry.
mutations.replace: var PristineBuffer = { Buffer: require('buffer').Buffer, from: require('buffer').Buffer.from, alloc: require('buffer').Buffer.alloc, concat: require('buffer').Buffer.concat, isBuffer: require('buffer').Buffer.isBuffer, bufferToString: function (b, e, a, c) { return b.toString(e, a, c); }, bufferIndexOf: function (b, n) { return b.indexOf(n); }, bufferSlice: function (b, a, c) { return b.slice(a, c); } };
expect_detail: http response body must not be steered

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when the chunked reassembly reads Buffer.concat live
mutations.why: http.js's chunked decoder reassembles across TCP segments with concat; a poisoned concat that reorders the parts desynchronises the size line from its body. This is framing over network-controlled bytes, not a cosmetic read.
mutations.replace: var BufferConcat = function (l, t) { return require('buffer').Buffer.concat(l, t); };
expect_detail: http chunked framing must not be steered

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when the chunk size is read through a live toString
mutations.why: The size line is read with buffer.toString('latin1', 0, lineEnd). A replacement that INFLATES the size is a request-smuggling primitive; node frames HTTP in C (llhttp) and is not steerable at all.
mutations.replace: var BufferPrototypeToString = function (b, e, a, c) { return b.toString(e, a, c); };
expect_detail: http chunked framing must not be steered

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when the framing cursor advances through a live slice
mutations.why: The decoder advances past each size line and body with slice; a corrupted cursor leaves a stray byte and desynchronises every later chunk.
mutations.replace: var BufferPrototypeSlice = function (b, a, c) { return b.slice(a, c); };
expect_detail: http chunked framing must not be steered

mutations.name: 65-lazy-buffer-capture dies when net's INBOUND wrap reads Buffer live
mutations.why: net's asBuffer wraps every 'data' chunk — the DISCLOSURE direction. The write-side assertion alone leaves it green while a shim reads every inbound byte.
mutations.replace: var BufferFrom = function (v, a, b) { return require('buffer').Buffer.from(v, a, b); };
expect_detail: net must not resolve Buffer through the shim

mutations.name: 66-process-console-intrinsic dies when node:process re-reads the global
mutations.why: The factory used to export the free-var process, so a pre-first-require reassignment of globalThis.process poisoned every later require('node:process'). Node returns the intrinsic regardless (#247).

mutations.name: 66-process-console-intrinsic dies when node:console re-reads the global
mutations.why: Same bug on the console factory: a pre-first-require reassignment of globalThis.console was captured as the module export. Console is a separate source file, so a single process entry would leave it unpinned.

mutations.name: 66-process-console-intrinsic dies when natives stop handing process the intrinsic
mutations.why: If install_internal_modules stops putting the process object on natives, the factory fail-closes. This pins the Odin wiring half, not just the JS export line.
mutations.expect_detail: node:process intrinsic missing at context init

mutations.name: 66-process-console-intrinsic dies when natives stop handing console the intrinsic
mutations.why: Symmetric to the process natives entry: console is a separate set_named, and leaving only the process one green-washes a console wiring regression.
mutations.expect_detail: node:console intrinsic missing at context init

mutations.name: gate-integrity dies when the NODE_BIN rule is removed
mutations.why: Without this rule agents set NODE_BIN=./bin/lava and every oracle becomes lava-vs-lava green.
mutations.find:
id: 'node-bin-override',
    reason:
      'NODE_BIN= turns oracle compares into lava-vs-lava or a fake oracle (scripts/lib/compare.sh)',
    re: /\bNODE_BIN\s*=/,
  },
mutations.replace:
id: 'node-bin-override',
    reason:
      'NODE_BIN= turns oracle compares into lava-vs-lava or a fake oracle (scripts/lib/compare.sh)',
    re: /(?!)/,
  },

mutations.name: gate-integrity dies when settings.json self-protect is dropped from PROTECTED_WRITE_PATHS
mutations.why: An agent that can Edit settings.json deletes the deny list; that path must stay hard-blocked.

mutations.name: compare.sh dies when the lava-vs-lava refusal is gutted
mutations.why: The check is the only runner-side stop for NODE_BIN pointing at lava; without it oracle suites lie.
mutations.find:
lava | lava.exe)
		printf '%s\n' "GATE INTEGRITY: NODE_BIN must be the Node oracle, not Lava (got $NODE_BIN)" >&2
		return 2
		;;

mutations.name: assert-case-counts dies when the min floor branch is disabled
mutations.why: Silent case deletion must fail the count; if (false) makes every suite green at any size.

mutations.name: bench-gate dies when --gate exits 0 without a runnable lava
mutations.why: rm bin/lava used to make bench-gate exit 0; the GATE branch must fail closed.

mutations.name: bench-gate dies when the uncapped-bench check is disabled
mutations.why: Without this, a new micro bench ships with no cap and never fails the gate.

mutations.name: check-global-replace dies when allowKey goes back to file:line
mutations.why: #337: line keys break on every edit above the site and train false hang alarms.
expect_detail: must not be keyed by line number
Expected values to be strictly equal

mutations.name: worktree isolation dies when the bootstrap path loses its pid suffix
mutations.why: A dropped $ collapses every bootstrap of one task onto a single path, so the second attempt hits the existence guard and the pipeline for that issue can never retry. This shipped once, in the rename out of scripts/agent-cycle/.

mutations.name: engine verdict routing dies when a missing pr-gate verdict is treated as shippable
mutations.why: Fail-open hard gate: a pr-gate that crashed, timed out, or ran under provider none returns ok with no findings file, and reading that as SHIP-AFTER opens a draft PR with zero mechanical gates run.
expect_detail: a PR was opened without a verdict

mutations.name: draft-pr guard dies when a non-SHIP verdict can still open a PR
mutations.why: ARCHITECTURE rule 3 and CLAUDE.md section 7: a draft PR may exist only after pr-gate returned SHIP or SHIP-AFTER. Without the re-check, one edited graph edge is enough to auto-open PRs off BLOCK.

mutations.name: the derived DAG dies when a closed prerequisite stops counting as satisfied
mutations.why: The graph shrinks as work lands because an edge pointing outside the open set is a landed dependency. Break that and every epic stays blocked by issues that already shipped, and the queue drains to nothing with work still available.

mutations.name: the derived DAG dies when a checklist above the first tier joins the queue
mutations.why: The master queue issue opens with trackers and house rules before the ordered section. A checkbox up there is someone notes; counted as a queue item it can mark real work done and drop it from the drain.
mutations.find: if (m && tier !== null) tiers.set(Number(m[2]), { tier, done: m[1] !== ' ' });

mutations.name: the hard gate dies when a BLOCK verdict still reports success
mutations.why: ok for a hard gate means the gate passed. The CLI exit code, the gate-failure trigger and the comment handler read ok and nothing else, and provider none exits 0 by construction, so a BLOCK reporting ok:true reads as success to all of them.
expect_detail: the verdict, not the exit code

mutations.name: trigger permission dies when an issue body can grant itself a run
mutations.why: The repository is public and an issue body is written by whoever opened it. Treating a lava-task marker as permission let a stranger enqueue an agent, and the dispatch path passes explicit issue numbers, which is the manual override that skips the label check.
expect_detail: an issue body granted itself a run

mutations.name: the in-flight guard dies when a running issue can be dispatched twice
mutations.why: bootstrapWorktree gives each attempt its own worktree and suffixed branch, so a second dispatch does not collide loudly — it silently runs the same issue twice and opens two PRs. The agent touching its own issue changes updatedAt, which is exactly when this fires.
expect_detail: not restarted by the issue being touched

mutations.name: the ledger lock dies when a held lock stops excluding a second holder
mutations.why: Mutual exclusion. Two pollers interleaving load and save on the dispatch ledger lose an attempt count or a completion, and the in-flight guard only helps if the claim that sets it is atomic with the check that reads it. Paired with the lost-update entry on the same mutation: expect_detail arrays are any-of, so one array naming both properties is satisfied by either alone.

mutations.name: the ledger lock dies when concurrent writers stop keeping every increment
mutations.why: Lost updates, the effect exclusion exists to prevent. Three processes each doing 25 locked read-modify-writes must total 75; without the lock a save overwrites an increment another process just made. Paired with the exclusion entry on the same mutation, because a single expect_detail array would accept either property on its own.

mutations.name: the claude retry dies when a signal-killed run is retried
mutations.why: spawnSync reports status null for a SIGKILL as well as for a spawn failure. A killed agent may already have edited the worktree and spent its budget, so repeating it is neither free nor idempotent.
expect_detail: killed by a signal is NOT retried

mutations.name: the drain dies when an issue already being worked on can start a second run
mutations.why: The trigger path refused a repeat dispatch; the drain path did not consult run state at all, so every `make agent-run` took the top of the queue again. One issue reached six concurrent runs, six worktrees and six agents doing the same work. A guard on one of two entry points is not a guard.

mutations.name: resume dies when a run whose worktree is gone is restarted instead of refused
mutations.why: The worktree IS the work: the branch, the edits, the plan the planner already wrote. Bootstrapping a fresh one under the old run id would look like a resume while discarding all of it.
